newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bahn plans to cut rail network - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bahn plans to cut rail network - magazine.

text.p: German state railway Deutsche Bahn AG said on Sunday it is examining the possibility of cutting back the country's extensive rail network by dismantling or selling off unprofitable sections of track.

A spokesman for Deutsche Bahn confirmed a report in the news magazine Spiegel which said that the group had undertaken a study to examine the economic viability of the network, which had identified loss-making sections.

A report in an advance copy of Spiegel said that around a quarter of the current rail network, around 10,000 kilometres is currently unprofitable and that the railway company plans to look for new operators for these sections of the network or close them down.
However, the Deutsche Bahn spokesman denied a decision to shut down or sell of sections of railway had already been made.
"Government reform of the railways in 1994 gave us the job of cutting costs in the network," the spokesman said, and said the company would try to improve the network on that basis.
It was possible that sections of the railway would be passed on to third-party operators, but shutting down lines and stations could only be seen as a last resort, he said.
The Spiegel report said that it costs around 75,000 marks a year to maintain one kilometre of railtrack, which amounts to total costs of around three billon marks a year.
